rationale:
Evidence from iteration 6 (kd 0.9, kp 3.0, base_speed 1.1, iteration 4 sensor spread; score 669.1, the best so far). The oval finished 20 of 20 at 1.96 s with max_error 0.015 and no line losses. The s-bend finished 18 of 20 with steering_oscillation 0.40, so kd 0.9 is at the edge of the useful range. The slalom still finished 0 of 20 with max_error 0.0634, which is above the 0.06 m limit, and 1.3 line-loss events per run. rms_error is low everywhere (0.006 to 0.018), so the failures are edge excursions on the slalom's sharp alternating bends, not poor average tracking.

What has been ruled out for the slalom: speed (1.2 to 1.1 gave no gain), a wider sensor spread (iteration 5 made the s-bend worse and did not fix the slalom), and kd 0.8 to 0.9 (max_error only moved from 0.0613 to 0.0634). Body width cannot help, because the off-track limit with body_width 0.18 is only 0.0575 and so stays at 0.06. The remaining lever the Evaluator named is kp. I take the Evaluator's requested step: kp 3.0 to 2.8 with kd 0.9 held. Lower kp reduces the turn per unit of signal, which should cut the overshoot that is building up at the slalom's alternating bends. I keep kd 0.9 because the s-bend completion (18 of 20) and oscillation (0.40) are still acceptable. The iteration 4 sensor spread, base_speed 1.1, ki 0, sensor_weights and line_loss 'last_direction' are unchanged, so the race isolates the kp effect.

Expected result: slalom max_error below 0.06 with line_loss_events falling toward 0.5, and some slalom finishes. Risk: less corrective turn on the tightest s-bend curves could cut s-bend completions, and the slalom could still fail if kp is the wrong lever. Measurements to check next: slalom max_error and line_loss_events; s-bend completion and steering_oscillation (revert kd to 0.8 if oscillation exceeds 0.4); oval completion_time.
